findings.message: 8 eyebrow/kicker label(s) above headings: "Vettri IT: manage every company laptop" (pill) above "HR and IT management in one platform"; "HR management" (pill) above "Everything HR needs, in one place"; "IT management · Built in" (pill) above "Every company laptop, managed from your "; "Product tour" (pill) above "See how it works"; "Ask Vettri AI" (pill) above "Answers for your team, without emailing "
findings.fix: Delete them. If the label carried real information, fold it into the headline or the supporting sentence.

findings.message: 5 gradient fill(s): div.v-hero__glow → linear-gradient(110deg, rgb(65, 105, 225), rgb(99, 102, 241) 35%, rgb(139, 92, 246) 65%, rgb(6, 182, 212)) | section#it.v-section.v-it → radial-gradient(50% 40% at 50% 0px, rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.35), rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) 75%), linear-gradient(rgb(10, 1 | div.v-it__glow → linear-gradient(110deg, rgb(65, 105, 225), rgb(99, 102, 241) 35%, rgb(139, 92, 246) 65%, rgb(6, 182, 212))
findings.fix: Use a flat colour or a real image. The only gradient allowed by default is a neutral scrim over a photo for legibility.

findings.message: 27 box-shadow(s) on elements at rest: a.v-pill → rgba(16, 24, 40, 0.05) 0px 1px 2px 0px | a.v-btn.v-btn--primary → rgba(16, 24, 40, 0.12) 0px 1px 2px 0px, rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.85) 0px 10px 26px - | a.v-btn.v-btn--secondary → rgba(16, 24, 40, 0.05) 0px 1px 2px 0px
findings.fix: Remove. Separate surfaces with a tone step or space. Shadows are for things that really float (menus, dialogs, sticky bars).

findings.message: Buttons with gradient fill and shadow/glow.
8 thin rule(s)/divider line(s): div.v-browser 807px | div.v-browser__bar 763px | div.v-browser__bar 984px | section#tour.v-section.v-section--canvas 1440px
findings.fix: Delete. Separate with space, a tone change, or scale. Lines are only for real tables and form fields.
Define a surface by its fill (one tone step from the page) or leave the content unboxed.
One blurred sticky bar at most; glass cards are a tell.
A page needs about five: display, heading, lead, body, small.

findings.message: The running text is a soft grey on its ground (5.9:1).
findings.fix: Set body copy in the full ink (7:1 or more). Keep the muted ink for secondary notes; pages read thin and unfinished when everything is grey.

findings.message: No video anywhere on the page.
findings.fix: Look for one honest clip with scripts/assets.mjs --video (the place, the material, the process) and use it as a muted loop with a poster frame. Defend its absence only if no clip fits the subject.

findings.message: Longest paragraph runs about 123 characters per line.

findings.fix: Nothing meant to be read goes below 13px.

findings.message: The first screen has no dominant element: the largest type is 64px (4.4vw) and no single picture holds a third of the viewport.
findings.fix: Make one thing lead: the headline at display size, or one large picture. A grid of many small pictures is not one thing; in blind tests jurors marked a first screen without a headline down every time. On the strongest studied sites the largest type has a median of 8.4vw.

findings.message: The same large text stays on screen for 4 screens in a row: "Ready to simplify HR and IT?"
findings.fix: A pinned element earns two screens, and something must change at each. Shorten the run or give every screen its own content.

findings.message: 2 headline(s) wrap past two lines at 390px: "HR and IT management in one platform" → 3 lines (7 words, 38px); "Every company laptop, managed from your HR app" → 3 lines (8 words, 30px)
findings.fix:
Cut words first (a headline is a title, not a sentence). Then give it a wider measure. Lower the size only as a last resort and never below the scale you chose. A real statement paragraph belongs in a

or

at 24px or less.
Vary the composition; not every section is a card grid.

findings.message: 1 row(s) scroll sideways with content past their edge.
findings.fix: Jurors and most visitors read a row cut at the edge as clipped, not as scrollable. Wrap it onto more lines, or end it inside the grid.
